hotel.name: Dan Eilat
hotel.address: HaYam Street 4, North Beach, Eilat, Israel

restaurants.name: Les Sardines
restaurants.description: A French-inflected fish bistro right on the North Marina, a couple of minutes' walk from the hotel, built around the daily catch grilled or oven-cooked simply. Excellent keto fit: whole grilled fish, seafood carpaccio, and meat mains dominate the menu, with pasta and bread as the only things to skip; strong enough as a full menu that non-keto companions are well covered too.

restaurants.name: Giraffe Noodle Bar
restaurants.description: A pan-Asian noodle bar directly on the promenade, serving pad thai, fried rice, dim sum, and wok skewers. Most of the menu is built around noodles and rice, which is the opposite of keto-friendly, but a handful of skewer and salad dishes can be ordered protein-forward on request — a reasonable backup, not a first choice, for the keto diner in the group.

restaurants.name: Ranch House
restaurants.description: A kosher American-style steakhouse and grill at the Royal Beach Hotel, next door to Dan Eilat. It's a straightforward high-fat, low-carb-friendly option rather than a specialty keto restaurant — a normal grill menu heavy on steaks and skewers, with fairly little for a vegetarian companion, which keeps it from scoring as high as the more varied fish-and-meat menus nearby despite the solid rating.

restaurants.name: Pastory
restaurants.description: Eilat's top-rated restaurant, an Italian Tuscan-style courtyard serving meat, seafood and housemade pasta side by side — entrecote, beef filet, and a seafood spaghetti alongside plenty of grilled fish and meat mains. The best of both worlds for a keto diner traveling with non-keto company: rich, high-fat proteins are the menu's centerpiece, and pasta lovers are just as well served.

restaurants.name: Eddie's Hideaway
restaurants.description: Eilat's oldest restaurant (since 1979), a French-American meat, fish and seafood house a short drive inland from the hotel strip, with foie gras, carpaccio, and a long list of grilled fish and steaks. A very solid keto option thanks to the sheer depth of high-fat, low-carb mains, and the pasta and children's menu mean non-keto diners in the group are covered too.

restaurants.name: The Last Refuge
restaurants.description: A 30-year-old fish-and-seafood institution on Almog Beach at the southern edge of a comfortable drive, known for grilled Red Sea fish and rich seafood platters with mussels, calamari, and lobster. Good keto fit on the fish and seafood side, but the menu leans heavily maritime with less to offer a non-seafood-eating companion than the more varied spots closer to the hotel.
